publication: MEDIC News (newsletter of MEDIC Enterprises, Inc. - Minority, Economic, Development, Industrial and Cultural Enterprises, Inc.)
date: circa April 1971 (Vol. 1, Issue 1; references SBA lending ceiling reached 'late November of last year' and a Manpower workshop-conference April 23-24, envelope postmarked Apr 23 1971)
summary: Launch issue of MEDIC News, an 8-page Newark community-economic-development newsletter. Lead article on MEDIC's mission to build black capitalism in Newark, quoting Sen. Edward W. Brooke from Black Enterprise magazine; describes MEDIC's founding in September 1968, its federal/state funding via the Economic Development Administration, Dept. of Community Affairs, and its designation as an Office of Minority Business Enterprise (OMBE) affiliate after a visit from Secretary of Commerce Maurice H. Stans. Editor's note from Carolyn Odom explains the newsletter's aim to document minority economic development honestly, invoking 'the black journals of the early 1800's.' Features a profile of MEDIC Press, Inc. (subsidiary print shop founded July 1969 with donated letterpress equipment). Profiles Tri-Cities Limo Service, a MEDIC-financed airport limousine business founded by two Passaic residents. Profiles board chairman William A. Mercer ('Engagement or Commitment' feature). Business-advice column 'Starting Your Own Business' by Thomas J. Greene. News items: Mayor Kenneth Gibson's Overall Economic Development Program (OEDP) Committee; Arch S. Whitehead named director of the state's minority enterprise program; First Annual Manpower Workshop-Conference (April 23-24) at Ebony Manor, Newark. Community activities calendar (BICC meeting, ICBO training courses, CMDNJ health forum). Masthead lists officers/executive committee and 29-member board.

incidents.what: MEDIC Enterprises, Inc. founded and incorporated as a New Jersey non-profit corporation
MEDIC Press, Inc. founded with $9,000 of donated letterpress equipment
Secretary of Commerce Maurice H. Stans visited Newark to designate MEDIC Enterprises an OMBE affiliate
SBA reached its statutory lending and guarantee ceiling, halting most minority business loans
MEDIC Press grossed close to $45,000 in sales and acquired ~$30,000 in fixed assets
Tri-Cities Limo Service launched with a $48,000 First Jersey National Bank loan (90% SBA guarantee) plus $5,300 from MEDIC
First Annual Manpower Workshop-Conference held at Ebony Manor, Newark, on 'Newark's Manpower Needs: New Directions for the 70's'
Mayor Kenneth A. Gibson appointed a 31-member Overall Economic Development Program (OEDP) Committee for Newark
Arch S. Whitehead named director of New Jersey's State Minority Enterprise Program

connections: Editor Carolyn Odom frames MEDIC News as heir to 'the black journals of the early 1800's', an explicit self-placement in Black press tradition

TRENDCO (Trenton Development Corporation) and BPUM (Black People's Unity Movement, Camden) named as sibling minority development corporations funded alongside MEDIC Enterprises under the same $2.5 million Office of Economic Opportunity grant
MEDIC Press, Inc. (MEDIC's print subsidiary) is itself a Black-owned Newark publishing/printing operation with capacity to enter the publishing field
